page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core and decompression capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average tier. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 254.5 GB/sec, while write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain average. In language model tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speed for small 135M models at 345.71 tokens/sec, though prompt processing speeds are average.

Given the inclusion of an NVIDIA L4 GPU and a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core, this server offers a resource-dense profile for workloads that require hardware acceleration without massive multi-core CPU overhead. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is suited for light LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, GPU-accelerated data processing, and memory-intensive analytical workloads.
description: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated and memory-intensive workloads. It is equipped with 12 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. The server features top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, alongside strong large-block memory read bandwidth. Text generation for small language models is highly efficient, reaching top-tier speeds. However, multi-core CPU performance and database operations remain in the average tier. With no bundled local storage, this instance requires external storage solutions. It is best suited for machine learning inference, GPU-accelerated data analysis, and memory-heavy applications.
